reason: shared_batch_judge_aggregator_crashes_on_bare_int_parse

## Traceback (excerpt from /workspace/logs/issue-778.log)

```
File "/workspace/explore-persona-space/src/explore_persona_space/eval/batch_judge.py", line 428, in <listcomp>
    valid = [s for s in scores if s.get("aligned") is not None and not s.get("error")]
                                  ^^^^^
AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'get'
```

## Root cause (verified by direct code inspection at `origin/main` and the pod)

- `issue778_lib.graded_judge` (plan-mandated graded 0-100 judge with drop-never-coerce) calls the sanctioned `eval.batch_judge.judge_completions_batch` (CLAUDE.md batch-judge-client rule).
- `judge_completions_batch` shells out to `parse_judge_json` per response. `parse_judge_json` returns `json.loads(text)` verbatim — for the persona-vectors rubric (`{"score": 42}` or a bare integer, per llm-judging.md rule 6 anchored 0-100 scale) it can return an `int` when the judge emits `"85"` alone.
- Then `_aggregate_persona_scores` (batch_judge.py:412-449, Betley-schema legacy) iterates every parsed entry and unconditionally calls `s.get("aligned")` (line 428) → `AttributeError` when `s` is an int.

The Betley legacy schema (`{"aligned": N, "coherent": N, "error": bool}`) is hard-wired into `_aggregate_persona_scores`; the persona-vectors rubric shape (bare int or `{"score": N}`) is fundamentally incompatible with that aggregator. This is the load-bearing shared-library incompatibility every `judge_completions_batch` caller with a non-Betley rubric will hit.

## Impact on this run

- Extract phase (Phase 1): DONE, artifacts intact on pod (`data/issue_778/{activations,rb,extract}`). 3 r_B vectors computed for evil/sycophancy/hallucination.
- Monitor phase (Phase 2): on-policy generation DONE (2000 rollouts × 3 traits already sent to Anthropic Batch API as `msgbatch_01X4uZ...`, `msgbatch_012upF...`, `msgbatch_01EgpqU...`). CRASH is in the JUDGE AGGREGATION step, AFTER submission. Batch results are still processing on Anthropic's side (per llm-judging.md batch caching rule, once they complete they land in the cache dir and a rerun re-uses them — no re-submission $$$).
- Finetune phase (Phase 3): NOT STARTED. Same judge path in the plan; will hit the same crash without a fix.

## Proposed fix (planner/implementer discretion — sketch)

Two minimum-diff options in decreasing order of preference:

1. **`_aggregate_persona_scores` graceful-skip on non-dict entries** — check `isinstance(s, dict)` at the top of the comprehension; treat non-dict as invalid (not counted toward `n_samples`, not counted toward the mean sums). This is a one-line guard that keeps Betley callers unchanged while allowing persona-vectors-style callers to complete without crashing. Legit for the library because the Betley-schema aggregation is skipped for non-Betley rubrics (which have no `aligned`/`coherent` fields anyway); the caller (`issue778_lib.graded_judge`) does its OWN aggregation from `all_scores`, so batch_judge's internal aggregator returning empty per-persona rows for persona-vectors callers is exactly right.

2. **Add an optional `parser`/`agg_skip=True` param to `judge_completions_batch`** to route persona-vectors-shape callers around `_aggregate_persona_scores` entirely. Broader but cleaner long-term contract.

Add a regression test: `tests/test_batch_judge_agg_non_dict_parse.py` — assert `judge_completions_batch` completes when `parse_judge_json` returns a bare int for one entry.

## Background

The promoted headline said the persona vector predicts trait expression no better than a norm-matched random direction. Three independent audits (markers v58–v64) established that the round-1/2 stochastic nulls were CIRCULAR: both were sampled from cov(pooled pos+neg extraction activations), whose top eigenvector is nearly parallel to r_B itself (cos 0.993 / 0.989 / 0.956 for evil / sycophancy / hallucination) — the "random" draws were near-copies of the direction under test. The user-approved round 3 re-extracted r_B faithfully per the released `generate_vec.py` (coherence gate ≥50 both arms, single paired mask; kept pairs 636 / 518 / 78), captured a 500-prompt neutral covariance, and recomputed both prediction experiments against a trait-agnostic null ladder.

## Methodology (round delta)

Six trait-agnostic null families (isotropic / within-class arm-centered / negative-arm-only / neutral-corpus / r_B-projected-out / score-shuffle permutation), norm-matched to r_B v2 per layer, 10,000 seeded draws each, (b+1)/(m+1) one-sided p, BH within family across the 15 setting-cells, and a registered min-p FWER over the 12 monitoring headline cells (draw-index-paired independence joint null — conservative under positive cross-cell dependence; finetune cells excluded by an effect-size-only pre-declaration). Two layer regimes: fixed paper steering layers 20/20/16 (1-indexed; indices 19/19/15), resolved from the paper source and frozen before any per-layer result (PRIMARY), and selection-symmetric max-over-28 (secondary). Primary honest family diagnostic-gated per trait (within-class for evil; negative-arm for sycophancy + hallucination). Old circular nulls re-run at 1,000 draws as labeled reference rows only. Within-condition bootstrap-CI bug fixed at source (`null_battery.py`, commit c937aa4c4a, regression-tested). λ sensitivity swept at {0.05, 0.1, 0.2} — no verdict changes.

## Results claim

The v1 headline INVERTS. (1) Family-wise: the registered min-p FWER over the 12 monitoring cells is significant in EVERY honest family — adjusted p = 0.0013 (per-trait primary mix, negative-arm, r_B-projected-out, score-shuffle), 0.0025 (isotropic, neutral-corpus), 0.0037 (within-class); the declared headline conjunction (primary AND neutral-corpus) passes. (2) Per cell at the fixed layer: 6 of 12 monitoring cells beat both honest nulls at BH ≤ 0.05 — evil 3/4 (misses 8-prompt within, r = 0.23), sycophancy 3/4 (8-prompt pooled misses only neutral-corpus at BH 0.059), hallucination 0/4 (observed |r| 0.01–0.69 at layer 16; its signal peaks 0.66–0.84 at layers 21–23). Strictest read (all five covariance families, both regimes): evil many-shot pooled + within (r 0.68 / 0.69) and hallucination finetune (r 0.92, effect-size-only). Sycophancy finetune (r 0.73) does not clear honest bands (p 0.06–0.19, n = 24). (3) The faithful re-extraction changed per-cell |r| by ≤ 0.032 (direction cos v1↔v2 0.94–1.00) — the inversion is entirely the null correction. (4) Re-run circular nulls still read p ≥ 0.05 in 10 of 15 cells; reference-only.

## Confidence

MODERATE. For: frozen fixed layers + registered multiplicity control, 10,000 draws, λ-robust, faithful extraction verified, conservative joint null. Against: single model; monitoring cells share eval questions (handled conservatively, not modeled); hallucination rests on 78 kept pairs and heavy judge drops; ICL exemplars reconstructed; finetune leg n = 24 and effect-size-only; judge-based DV (validated ρ(graded, binary) 0.98/0.91/0.97).
